title: Deployment Pipelines
description: Build reliable, automated deployment pipelines for Linux servers using Git, CI/CD tools, and blue-green or canary release strategies.

data.text: A deployment pipeline is the automated path from code commit to production. When pipelines are fast, safe, and repeatable, teams ship improvements weekly instead of quarterly.
This lesson covers Git-based pipelines, Linux server deployment patterns, and release strategies that reduce risk without slowing down delivery.
A typical pipeline has four stages: build, test, package, and deploy. Each stage must pass before the next begins. If any stage fails, the pipeline stops and alerts the team.

items: Build: compile code and create artifacts
Test: run unit, integration, and security tests
Package: containerize or archive the release
Deploy: push to staging or production with verification

data.title: GitHub Actions workflow for Linux deployment
data.code:
name: Deploy to Linux

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - run: npm run build
      - uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.SERVER_HOST }}
          username: deploy
          key: ${{ secrets.SSH_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          script: |
            cd /var/www/app
            git pull origin main
            npm ci --production
            pm2 reload app

data.text: Releasing to all users at once is risky. Blue-green and canary releases reduce risk by validating changes with a subset of traffic before rolling out fully.

rows: Route 5% of traffic to new version

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Start with rolling updates and health checks. Add canary releases only when your monitoring is reliable enough to detect a bad release before most users see it.
Trunk-based development pairs naturally with automated pipelines. Developers merge small, frequent changes to main, and feature flags hide incomplete work. Long-lived branches become unnecessary.

items: Merge to main daily, not weekly
Use short-lived feature branches under one day old
Hide unfinished features behind feature flags
Automate builds and tests on every push
Require manual approval for production deployments
Implement health checks after every deploy
Use blue-green or canary releases for critical services
Track deployment frequency and failure rate in a dashboard

data.title: Summary
data.text: Deployment pipelines turn code commits into reliable production releases. Automate every stage, validate with tests, and choose a release strategy that matches your team's maturity. Ship small, ship often, and monitor every deployment.
